## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

**You are eligible for Child Benefit for 2 out of 3 children.**

### ✅ **Alex (ELIGIBLE)**
You can claim Child Benefit for Alex even though they are 20 years old and have been in hospital for 13 weeks. While Child Benefit normally stops after 12 weeks in hospital, there's an important exception: you can continue receiving it if you regularly spend money on the child. Since you do regularly spend money on Alex, you qualify for this exception.

### ❌ **Blake (INELIGIBLE)**
You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Blake for two main reasons:
1. Blake works 24+ hours per week and is not in approved education - this disqualifies them from Child Benefit
2. Blake doesn't live with you and you contribute £0.00 towards their upkeep. To claim Child Benefit for a child living elsewhere, you must contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.)

### ✅ **Charlie (ELIGIBLE)**
You can claim Child Benefit for Charlie. At 5 years old, Charlie meets all the standard criteria: under 16, lives with you, and has no disqualifying factors.

**Next Steps:** You should apply for Child Benefit for Alex and Charlie. Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, so make sure no one else is claiming for them.

But there is an exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit for children in a UK hospital if you regularly spend money on them. Since you regularly spend money on Alex, this exception applies. Alex also does not work 24+ hours/week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits. Therefore, you remain ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex despite being over 16 and in hospital for 13 weeks, because you regularly spend money on them.

Blake is 16 years old and has left education or training, having been registered with a government-sponsored careers service for less than 20 weeks. Under the rules, you can get Child Benefit for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service. This would normally make Blake eligible. However, Blake does not live with you and you pay £0.00 towards their upkeep. To qualify for Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you, you must be paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them (on food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Since you're contributing £0.00, you do not meet this requirement. Additionally, Blake works 24+ hours/week and is not in approved education, which is a disqualifying factor. Therefore, you are INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Blake.

Charlie is 5 years old (under 16), lives with you, is not in local authority care, not in hospital or residential accommodation, not fostered, does not work 24+ hours/week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits. Charlie meets all the standard eligibility criteria: under 16, lives with you (so you're responsible for them), and has no disqualifying factors. You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Charlie.
